title: Lichtenbaum's special-value programme in the agenda
notes: Plan item 4 announces \ru{Гипотеза Лихтенбаума} connecting \(\zeta\)-values at integers with higher \(K\)-theories; Manin is the prospective expositor.
statement: No field, scheme, integer range, leading-term convention, regulator or torsion factor is specified. A programme relating special values and algebraic \(K\)-groups is identifiable, but a unique quantified conjecture is not.
fate: \citet{lichtenbaum1973values} is a contemporary thematic match: Seattle conference 1972, publication 1973. The notes do not identify a particular conjecture of that paper.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The agenda sentence has no single solved/open truth value and is not a definite problem.

title: Finite generation of the two function-field families
notes: For finite \(k\), the notes assert finite generation of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(k[t])\), \(n\geq3\), and \(\mathrm{SL}_n(k[t,t^{-1}])\), \(n\geq2\).
statement: For every finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), both families are finitely generated in the displayed ranges.
fate: The pre-1973 result is credited to Behr 1969 and Harder's reduction theory in \citet[p.~312]{buxkohlwitzel2013rank}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established. Finite generation alone does not imply finite presentation.

title: Serre's finite-presentation question over a polynomial ring
statement: For every prime power \(q\) and integer \(n\geq3\), determine finite presentability of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb F_q[t])\).
fate: No at \(n=3\); yes at \(n\geq4\). The Rank Theorem gives finiteness length \(n-2\) \citep[p.~312]{buxkohlwitzel2013rank}. It credits the complete finite-presentation criterion to Behr 1998. General-rank preprint 2011, final 2013; these are not asserted to be first dates for each special case.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Completely answered, including small finite fields.

title: Serre's finite-presentation question over a Laurent ring
notes: The same question is posed for \(\mathrm{SL}_n(k[t,t^{-1}])\), \(k\) finite, \(n\geq2\).
statement: For every finite field \(\mathbb F_q\) and integer \(n\geq2\), determine finite presentability of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb F_q[t,t^{-1}])\).
fate: The rank sum is \(2(n-1)\), and finiteness length \(2n-3\): no at \(n=2\), yes at \(n\geq3\) \citep[p.~312]{buxkohlwitzel2013rank}. The complete finite-presentation criterion was already established by Behr 1998.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Completely answered. Replacing \(\mathbb F_q\) by \(\mathbb Z\) changes the problem.

title: Coherence of a group
notes: \ru{Когер. группа}: every subgroup with finitely many generators is finitely presented.
statement: A group \(G\), not necessarily finitely generated, is coherent when every finitely generated subgroup \(H\leq G\) is finitely presented.
fate: This is the group-theoretic property in Serre's questions \citep[pp.~734--735]{serre1974problems}. Requiring the ambient group to be finitely presented would improperly exclude the question about \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Q)\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Standard terminology; unrelated to sheaf or ring coherence.

title: Free groups are coherent
notes: The notes say that free groups are coherent.
statement: Every subgroup of a free group is free. A finitely generated such subgroup has finite rank and a finite presentation with no relators.
fate: This is the classical Nielsen--Schreier implication; free coherent groups are recalled in \citet[section~4]{brody2025commensurator}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established, even if the ambient free group has infinite rank.

title: Nilpotent groups are coherent
notes: The faint abbreviation following free is read as \ru{нильпот.}.
statement: Every finitely generated subgroup of a nilpotent group is finitely generated nilpotent, hence polycyclic and finitely presented.
fate: This is the classical polycyclic implication; see the coherent classes recalled in \citet[section~4]{brody2025commensurator}. The scan supports the transmitted abbreviation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; torsion-freeness and finite generation of the ambient group are unnecessary.

title: Scott's coherence theorem for three-manifold groups
notes: The notebook explicitly cites Scott, JLMS(2)6(1973),437--440, for coherence of three-manifold fundamental groups.
statement: For a connected second-countable three-manifold \(M\), with or without boundary, every finitely generated subgroup of \(\pi_1(M)\) is finitely presented: apply Scott's theorem to the corresponding connected covering.
fate: \citet[section~2]{scott1973finitely} is the exact work, published May 1973, before this meeting. Its original introductory statement was read in the author's collected works.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established. The covering-space argument supplies the subgroup quantifier.

title: The imaginary-quadratic arithmetic example
notes: \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\Lambda)\) is called coherent, with \(\Lambda\) described as \ru{чисто мнимые элем. квадр. поля}.
statement: For an imaginary quadratic number field \(K\), \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal O_K)\) is coherent, where \(\mathcal O_K\) is its ring of integers.
reconstruction: Replacing the transmitted description by the ring of integers is a mathematical reconstruction, not a new reading of the ink.
fate: This is the expected Bianchi-group consequence of \citet{scott1973finitely}: use a torsion-free finite-index subgroup and stability of coherence under finite extensions.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The reconstruction is established. Purely imaginary elements themselves are not a unital coefficient ring.

title: Is SL3(Z) coherent?
notes: The notes explicitly ask whether \(\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\) is coherent.
statement: Is every finitely generated subgroup \(H\leq\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)\) finitely presented?
fate: The question remains explicit and open in \citet[p.~5]{audibert2025zariski}. Incoherence in ranks \(n\geq4\) does not answer it.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: No unconditional resolution was found in the dated search; the universal subgroup quantifier remains.
worth: Focused work on a specified subgroup family is worthwhile, but this run found no bounded route to full coherence.

title: Is SL2(Z[1/p]) coherent?
notes: The same line asks about \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z[1/p])\).
statement: For every prime \(p\), is every finitely generated subgroup of \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z[1/p])\) finitely presented?
reconstruction: The conventional assumption that \(p\) is prime is made explicit.
fate: \citet[Theorem~4.2, version~3]{brody2025commensurator} proves a conditional positive result from Greenberg--Shalom. First preprint 2023; checked revision 7 November 2025. The hypothesis is essential to the attribution.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Open unconditionally in the checked literature. Inverting two distinct primes is a different, negatively answered problem.
worth: A specified subgroup family may admit a bounded study; the required arithmeticity hypothesis and full coherence exceed the contribution justified here.

title: Coherence of GLn(Q)
notes: The line ends \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Q)?\), with no rank restriction.
statement: For which integers \(n\geq1\) is the abstract discrete group \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Q)\) coherent?
reconstruction: The rank 1 exception is explicit. The thesis's displayed Baumslag--Solitar label is not copied: conjugation by \(\operatorname{diag}(p/q,q/p)\) scales a unipotent entry by \((p/q)^2\).
fate: Yes at \(n=1\), no at \(n\geq2\). Baumslag's rational triangular obstruction is recorded with Serre's questions and discussed in \citet[p.~74]{brody2022trees}; block inclusion handles larger ranks.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Answered. Finitely generated subgroups of \(\mathbb Q^\times\) are finitely generated abelian. The printed resolution is traced to 1974; the exact date of Baumslag's intervening observation is unverified.
